public_rationale: The claim's testable core is that AI startups, as a group, pay OpenAI and Anthropic mainly with venture funding rather than with operating cash flow. The target period is 1 January to 8 September 2026. The packet has no aggregate or representative data on how AI startups funded their model spending in that period. The only evidence item is a PYMNTS report available on 4 September 2026 (e1). It says Cursor and GitHub Copilot drove about $1.2 billion of Anthropic's $5 billion revenue milestone in the prior year, and that GitHub is owned by Microsoft. That figure is for 2025, not the target period. It also does not describe any buyer's cash flow or funding sources. The evidence neither supports nor contradicts the claim.
limitations: 'Artificial' is a characterization. Only the claim that the payments depend on venture funding can be tested.
The packet has no cash-flow, funding, or margin data for any AI startup in 2026.
The only evidence item covers 2025 and names just two large customers of Anthropic. It says nothing about OpenAI's startup customers.
The packet does not show what share of the labs' revenue comes from AI startups as opposed to other customers.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI startups are an artificial source of revenue for AI labs because they pay with venture capital rather than cashflow.

statement.excerpt: AI startups are an artificial source of revenue.

from_speaker: AI startups are an artificial source of revenue
not paying Anthropic and OpenAI out of cashflow
only able to do so as long as somebody else hands them endless amounts of cash
our_interpretation: 'Artificial' is a characterization. The checkable core is that AI startups' payments to OpenAI and Anthropic are funded mainly by venture capital rather than by operating cash flow.
Read as a general claim about AI startups as a group, as the speaker frames it ('in virtually every case I've found'), not as a claim about every single startup.
He describes an ongoing state with no named period. The target period is 2026 up to the post date, the period the post's examples (Harvey's 2025 to 2026 raises) point to.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that most AI startups paying for model access run at operating losses or negative cash flow, and fund their token spending from venture raises.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that a substantial share of AI-startup spending with the labs comes from startups that generate positive operating cash flow, or that pay without depending on new venture funding.
